Approved same-name harness overrides take precedence and active agents adopt them at the next safe step. Preserve source/override provenance and version history. This resolves the previously open agent authority for editing shared skills: do not mutate shared originals as part of harness self-improvement.

decisions.source: User: Yes, support SQLite, MariaDB/MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, and HydraDB if indexable.
decisions.decision: Require SQLite, MariaDB/MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server for schema indexing and separately permissioned data tools, verifying both MariaDB and MySQL. HydraDB is conditional on indexability within the agreed scope and permissions. It does not replace HelixDB/SQLite app storage. Official HydraDB graph MCP documentation lacks a schema-discovery tool and uses unrestricted Cypher; read-only structural inference and enforcement require validation. Subsequent hydradb_readonly_structure_inspection approves read-only record inspection for schema inference with metadata-only retention; feasibility and read-only enforcement remain unvalidated. Versions, authentication and per-engine metadata coverage remain open.

decisions.source: User: Yes, read-only inspection to infer the structure is fine, as long as only schema metadata is retained, not actual data.
decisions.decision: Authorize read-only HydraDB graph-record inspection for structural inference. Retain only schema metadata, such as labels, property names/types and relationship types; no source records or property values may persist through the indexing path, including query results, diagnostics, logs, transcripts, artifacts, caches or embeddings. Report inferred versus declared metadata, coverage and freshness. Inspection must not mutate the source or confer write permission. Actual HydraDB discovery and enforceable read-only access remain unvalidated, so support stays conditional. This settles the discovery-scope question in database_target_engines; separately permissioned data tools retain their distinct scope.

decisions.source: User Yes to read-only database connections by default, with data writes requiring explicit enablement for each connection.
decisions.decision: Every configured target database connection defaults to read-only. The user must explicitly enable data writes for each connection; enabling one must not enable others. Connection write enablement remains subject to selected tool permissions and project scope and cannot grant code-review agents write access. Schema indexing and HelixDB structural inspection remain read-only regardless of data-tool write settings. This settles connection permission defaults and write-enable scope; schema-changing DDL authority is settled by database_schema_changes_prefer_committed_migrations. Enforcement details, transactions, limits and result retention remain to be resolved.

decisions.source: User: Preferably through committed migrations, but if that is not possible, yes, confirming schema changes on write-enabled connections.
decisions.decision: Allow schema-changing operations, preferring migration files committed to the appropriate project repository through normal worktree/review/delivery workflow. If committed migrations are not possible, direct schema changes are allowed. Applying either route requires explicit write enablement on the target connection plus agent tool permission and project scope; committing a migration does not itself authorize application. Indexing and reviewers remain read-only. Keep associated work/agent/action history. Recording the migration commit or fallback reason/outcome is proposed under DB-05; migration execution, transactions, retries and result retention remain implementation decisions.

decisions.source: User Shareable to connections being shared across projects with access controlled per project.
decisions.decision: Database connections may be shared by multiple projects, with access controlled per project. Sharing does not automatically grant access to other projects or their agents. At invocation, enforce requesting-project access together with connection policy and agent tool permissions. Project access cannot override a read-only connection; indexing and reviewers remain read-only. Keep project/agent action attribution. Reusing one connection definition across associations and showing effective access is proposed under DB-02; detailed permission configuration and enforcement remain to be specified.

decisions.source: User Skipped to the next occurrence of a scheduled inference task arriving while its previous run is still running.
decisions.decision: Skip overlapping scheduled inference occurrences. Do not start a duplicate run or queue catch-up for that occurrence. Preserve the active run and show the skipped outcome in history. Existing resume, explicit-pause and missed-occurrence policies remain effective.

decisions.source: User Yes, and default to ask me, confirming separate per-repository Automatic / Ask me / Disabled settings for agent-initiated deployments and release publishing, independent of Auto-Merge and with inherited defaults.
decisions.decision: Deployments and release publishing each have their own policy: Automatic, Ask me or Disabled. Both default to Ask me. Inherit workspace defaults through projects, with independent repository overrides and visible effective values/sources. Neither setting is implied by Auto-Merge or by the other setting. Ask me requires explicit approval before the action; Disabled prevents it; Automatic remains subject to tool permissions and execution rules. Harness self-install/restart retains its explicit approval requirement. Deployment target configuration, execution and approval-binding mechanics remain to be specified.

decisions.source: User selected managed executable language packs and explicitly requested optional .NET, TypeScript, Swift and Rust semantic indexers and an add-ons management screen.
decisions.decision: Downloadable prebuilt managed executable language packs extend the native Rust app without recompiling it. The app owns helper lifecycle and a versioned protocol; no separate administered server or VM is required. Provide optional semantic packs for .NET, TypeScript, Swift and Rust and a dedicated Settings Add-ons screen for installation, updates, enablement, removal, configuration, prerequisites, compatibility and diagnostics. Tree-sitter baseline remains independent. Accept SCIP and native-format adapters, including Swift index stores. Rust SDK, manifest/transport, distribution/trust, supported versions/platforms and active-run/update/rollback mechanics are proposed details, not yet validated integrations.

decisions.source: User requested capture of the Pi/Oh My Pi discussion and the proposed Rust harness package architecture in the requirements.
decisions.decision: General harness packages use managed executables and a Rust SDK, sharing the language-pack host and Add-ons management screen. Packages contribute tools, commands, workflows/gates, events, context/compaction, approved skills/prompts/role instructions, provider registrations through the router and host-rendered egui UI. Agents can build and test package projects, but agent-authored executable versions require user approval before activation. Reload approved versions at safe boundaries, preserve prior versions for guarded rollback and record package/version/work provenance. All brokered actions follow existing router, permissions, reviewer restrictions and work/review policies; process separation is not an OS security sandbox. Pi and Oh My Pi are design references. Oh My Pi has TypeScript/Bun agent and extension code plus Rust native tooling; direct compatibility with their existing packages is not selected. Exact SDK/protocol/UI contribution schemas, executable trust, distribution, hook failure/replay and state migration remain proposed details.

decisions.source: User: Yes, that is fine, just never force push to main, answering automatic own task branches versus approval for feature/main branches.
decisions.decision: Agents may automatically force-push their own task branches, such as after rebasing. Feature branches require explicit user approval. Main must never be force-pushed. Branches outside the agent-owned task scope do not gain automatic authority. Existing branch protections still apply. Expected-revision force-with-lease, concrete-target approval binding, ownership checks, equivalent refspec/tool enforcement and reconciliation are proposed implementation details.

decisions.source: User: Yes, all final PRs should pass checks and reviews before any are merged, then merge them in dependency order.
decisions.decision: For multi-repository features, every final feature PR must pass its required checks and reviews before any final PR is merged. Once all are ready, merge in dependency order, preserving effective per-repository merge authority and review policies. Partial-delivery failure/recovery remains open.

decisions.source: User: Do not notify me; resolve conflicts and continue. Concurrent agents in the same repository will often conflict. Pause and inform me if a merge fails in a completely unusual way.
decisions.decision: Routine merge conflicts, including conflicts caused by concurrent agents in the same repository or during multi-repository delivery, are resolved autonomously without user notification or routine approval. Continue under existing required checks, reviews and merge authority; never force-push main. Unusual merge failures the coordinator cannot resolve pause affected delivery and dependent work and notify the user, while independent work continues. Exact unusual-failure classification and recovery mechanics remain to specify; this is not approval for automatic reversal of successful merges.

decisions.source: User: Once all final PRs are merged. Releases and deployments should be tracked separately.
decisions.decision: A feature is complete when all final feature PRs are verified merged to main across its affected repositories. Release and deployment records have separate linked statuses and retain their independent configured policies; pending, approval-waiting or failed release/deployment work does not keep the feature open. Apply existing feature-completion cleanup with visible cleanup outcomes and retained history/artifacts.

decisions.source: User: Yes, that would be a nice addition, answering optional per-project keep-working mode that starts the next eligible feature or issue.
decisions.decision: Provide an optional per-project keep-working mode using project next_work priority/eligibility and normal Start policies. Expose mode state, controls and activity. Existing approvals, pauses, budgets, permissions, ownership and resource rules remain effective. Work-item concurrency is subsequently confirmed as one feature or standalone issue per project under keep_working_one_item_per_project. Manual restart after app closure is subsequently confirmed under keep_working_manual_restart. Stop when no eligible work remains is subsequently confirmed under keep_working_stop_without_eligible_work. Default off for new projects is subsequently confirmed under keep_working_default_off; do not infer a global subagent cap.

decisions.source: User: However, new work should always start in a new session with a clear context.
decisions.decision: Every newly started feature, standalone issue or task assignment gets a distinct session and context assembled specifically for that work, regardless of manual, scheduled or keep-working origin. Include relevant instructions, brief, project knowledge and scoped evidence without inheriting the prior work conversation as the new transcript. Preserve work/origin/history links. Continue of existing work retains its established history and continuity.

decisions.source: User: Just one feature at a time, answering one feature or issue per project versus configurable concurrent work items in keep-working mode.
decisions.decision: Keep-working mode runs one feature or standalone issue at a time per project. It does not introduce a configurable multi-item concurrency setting. The current item may still use its independent configured subagent allowance and useful task parallelism; other projects may work independently. Fresh-session rules apply to each next item. Manual restart after closure is subsequently confirmed under keep_working_manual_restart. Stop when no eligible work remains is subsequently confirmed under keep_working_stop_without_eligible_work. Default off for new projects is subsequently confirmed under keep_working_default_off.

decisions.source: User: yes, answering whether keep-working also requires manual restart after closing and reopening, matching manual Continue.
decisions.decision: After the application is closed and reopened, per-project keep-working remains stopped until the user manually restarts it. Do not automatically start new queued features or issues solely because the mode was active before closure. Existing work still requires selective manual Continue; restarting mode does not clear those holds. Maintenance/scheduled-job restart policies remain separate.

decisions.source: User: Stop, answering whether keep-working stays enabled and waits for eligible work or stops until enabled again.
decisions.decision: When keep-working seeks the next item and no eligible work remains, stop the mode rather than remain enabled watching the queue. Later work additions or eligibility changes must not reactivate it; require explicit manual enablement. Preserve existing work, pauses, approvals and history. This answer concerns the queue policy, not a request to stop the requirements interview.

decisions.source: User: Yes, answering whether keep-working is off by default for each new project.
decisions.decision: Keep-working is off by default for every newly created project and starts only after explicit user enablement. Retain one feature or standalone issue at a time per project, fresh sessions for new work, manual restart after app closure/reopening, and stopping when no eligible work remains until manually enabled again.

decisions.source: User: Yes, answering whether project removal archives records/history by default, with permanent deletion available as a separate explicit action.
decisions.decision: Default project removal archives its records and linked work/history rather than permanently deleting them. Make archived records accessible and provide permanent deletion as a distinct explicit action. UI and permitted agent tools share this behavior. Active-agent confirmation and immediate project-work stop are subsequently confirmed under archive_active_agents_confirm_immediate_stop. Manual reactivation after restoration is subsequently confirmed under restored_project_manual_reactivation. Stop verification, restoration controls, shared references and permanent-deletion mechanics remain to specify. The harness-only deletion boundary is subsequently confirmed under permanent_project_deletion_harness_only.

decisions.source: User: If active agents are working on a project being archived, warn the user and ask if they are sure. If yes, all work stops immediately; there is no point waiting for a safe stopping point.
decisions.decision: Before archiving a project with active agents, warn and require user confirmation. Declining leaves project/work unchanged. Confirmation immediately stops all project work and blocks new dispatch; do not wait for safe-step boundaries, completed tools/tasks or cooperative checkpoints. Apply to coordinators, subagents, inference/tools, owned processes and background work, preserving history and interrupted state. Archived projects cannot restart through schedules, keep-working or other dispatch paths; unrelated projects continue. Cancellation/stop verification and uncertain external-effect reconciliation require implementation detail; restoration leaves execution stopped until explicit manual reactivation, subsequently confirmed under restored_project_manual_reactivation.

decisions.source: User: Yes, answering whether restoring an archived project leaves its work and schedules stopped until manually reactivated.
decisions.decision: Restoring an archived project leaves work and agents, keep-working mode and project schedules stopped. Require explicit manual reactivation; restoration alone never resumes execution or bypasses existing pauses, approvals or budgets.

decisions.source: User: Yes, only delete the harness data and artifacts. Leave local repositories and GitHub resources untouched.
decisions.decision: Permanent project deletion removes only harness data and artifacts. Leave local repository files, worktrees and branches and all GitHub resources untouched; do not invoke Git cleanup or remote mutations as a side effect. Preservation of shared artifacts referenced by other projects is subsequently confirmed under preserve_artifacts_referenced_by_other_projects. Shared-data ownership and deletion mechanics remain open.

decisions.source: User: Many people have a preferred base directory for local repos; we should have that as a configuration setting.
decisions.decision: Provide a preferred base directory for local repositories in Settings. Directory chooser/path validation, default clone destinations, preserving existing paths and distinguishing worktree/artifact locations are proposed behavior; app-wide inheritance with optional project overrides is subsequently confirmed under repository_base_directory_project_overrides. Default path and naming remain open.

decisions.source: User: Yes, answering whether deleting one project preserves an artifact still referenced by another project.
decisions.decision: Permanent deletion of a project must preserve shared artifact contents and remaining-project references/access while another project still references the artifact. Do not treat a project deletion as authority to delete artifacts retained by another project. Shared-data ownership and exact deletion mechanics remain open.

decisions.source: User: Yes, and project overrides are a good idea.
decisions.decision: Preferred repository base directory is an app-wide default with optional per-project overrides. Projects without an override inherit the app-wide value; clearing an override restores inheritance.

decisions.source: User: Support choosing a preferred container system, Docker, Podman, and if possible Apple built-in container support on Macs.
decisions.decision: Add preferred container backend configuration with Docker and Podman support plus Apple first-party container tooling where feasible on supported Macs. Treat runtimes as optional project dependencies, retain Rust host implementation and detect/report prerequisites, unsupported capabilities and availability. Apple container is separately installed, not assumed preinstalled; official README currently requires Apple silicon and supports macOS 26. App-wide backend inheritance with optional project overrides is subsequently confirmed under container_backend_project_overrides. Initial default, Compose compatibility, operation coverage and lifecycle remain to refine.

decisions.source: User: Yes, answering whether the container backend uses an app-wide default with optional project overrides.
decisions.decision: Provide an app-wide preferred container backend with optional per-project overrides. Projects without an override inherit the app-wide backend; clearing an override restores inheritance. Preserve explicit backend selection, availability reporting and existing tool permissions.

decisions.source: User: Yes, answering whether app closure stops containers launched for agent work while leaving pre-existing or manually managed containers running.
decisions.decision: On app closure, stop containers launched for agent work; leave pre-existing and manually managed containers running. Target attributed agent-work containers, not the whole engine. Stopping does not authorize deletion of containers/images/volumes/data. Exact ownership detection, stop recovery and restart behavior remain open.

decisions.source: User: Help near Settings; every aspect of the working system must be documented, searchable and accessible by agents, including all UI and extensibility/plugin/add-in authoring.
decisions.decision: Provide a first-class Help menu/navigation destination near Settings. Maintain complete searchable documentation for the working system, every UI screen/action/setting and behavior, workflows, configuration, permissions and recovery. Document all supported extensibility points and how to create/test/package/install/manage harness packages, language packs, plugins and add-ins, with practical examples. Agents access the same maintained content through first-class read/search tools under existing permissions. Subsequently confirmed under help_local_offline_only_versioned: Help lives entirely offline/local, bundled and versioned with the installed app/add-ons. Every screen and Settings section now requires a contextual Help link under context_help_every_screen_settings. Error links and bounded retrieval remain proposed.

decisions.source: User: If agents are writing self-improvements to the harness, part of their work MUST require documentation.
decisions.decision: Every agent-authored harness self-improvement must include appropriate documentation with the work: affected Help/UI/tool behavior and developer/extension guides/examples. Include documentation in planning, acceptance, verification and review; missing, stale or incomplete required documentation blocks completion/delivery rather than becoming optional follow-up. Existing code/skill/role/package approval and activation rules remain effective.

decisions.source: User: Yes to bundling Help offline and versioning with the app/add-ons; Help will only live offline and local.
decisions.decision: Help lives entirely locally and offline, bundled and matched to installed app and add-on versions. Human Help browsing/search and agent search/read operate on the same local documentation without a hosted service, network requirement or remote search fallback. Exact local format/search/packaging mechanics remain open.

decisions.source: User: Auto update from GitHub Releases on the eventual hosting repo; poll every hour; show new version available for download in lower-left sidebar and always show current version there.
decisions.decision: Provide application updates from GitHub Releases on the SceneWorks/DevWorks repository, with automatic hourly polling while the app is open. Always display the installed version in the lower-left sidebar and indicate a newer release available for download in that same area with access to the update/download action. Downloaded or merely available releases do not replace the displayed installed version. The repository identity is not yet chosen. Automatic background downloads with explicit approval before installation/restart are subsequently confirmed under automatic_update_download_approved_install_restart. Release channels, first-check/recovery, artifact validation, platform installation and rollback mechanics remain open; existing self-improvement activation approval and shutdown/resume rules still apply.

decisions.source: User: Yes please, answering whether every screen and Settings section links to its relevant local Help topic.
decisions.decision: Every screen and Settings section must provide a contextual Help link opening the relevant local documentation topic. This is confirmed under HELP-01; contextual error links and exact topic identity/navigation mechanics remain proposed under HELP-06.

decisions.source: User: Yes, answering whether updates download automatically in the background with approval required before installation and restart.
decisions.decision: Automatically download new application updates in the background. Explicit user approval is required before installation/restart; discovery/download do not count as approval. Pending or declined approval leaves the running installed version in use and authorized work may continue. Approved updates preserve existing work/shutdown/selective-resume rules and version-matched local Help.

decisions.source: User: built-in RAG for vectorizing and searching knowledge from documents; users must be able to add their own knowledge documents for indexing.
decisions.decision: Built-in document ingestion, embedding/vector indexing and passage retrieval are required, including user-added knowledge documents. RAG-01 is confirmed. RAG-02–08 propose visible corpus management, format handling, hybrid search, provenance/citations, scoping, model/version-aware indexing, diagnostics and existing router/storage integration. Current-project default, explicit sharing and moving documents are subsequently confirmed under RAG-11. OxiRS is an evaluated reuse candidate, not selected infrastructure; preserve HelixDB/SQLite and router decisions pending evidence.

decisions.source: User: Yes, support Markdown, plain text, PDF and Word documents.
decisions.decision: Markdown, plain text, PDF and Word are required initial formats for user-added knowledge document ingestion, indexing and retrieval under RAG-09. Routed vision fallback for scanned/image-only pages is subsequently confirmed under RAG-10; vision extraction is subsequently confirmed on by default; modern .docx only is subsequently confirmed on 1 November 2026; extraction failures must be visible.

decisions.source: User: Yes, answering whether routed vision should be the configurable fallback for scanned pages.
decisions.decision: Extract existing text directly; use a configured vision-capable model via the internal router for scanned/image-only pages, configurable in Settings. Save and reuse source/page-linked extraction with model provenance until source change or explicit re-extraction, then chunk/embed separately through the router. No dedicated bundled OCR model/runtime is required for this pathway. Enabled by default, with a Settings control to disable it. Detailed rendering/quality mechanics remain open. Confirmed under RAG-10.

decisions.source: User: On by default, answering the default for routed vision extraction.
decisions.decision: Routed vision extraction fallback for scanned/image-only document pages is enabled by default, with a Settings control to disable it and configure its route/model. Existing router permissions, provider availability, usage attribution and visible partial/failure status remain effective. Confirmed under RAG-10.

decisions.source: User: Yes to current-project default and explicit sharing, plus moving documents to another project to correct accidental placement.
decisions.decision: Knowledge documents default to the current project. Provide explicit cross-project sharing and Move to project controls, including correction of misplaced uploads. Preserve identity, provenance and move history; future retrieval follows the new association and explicit sharing. UI and configured agent tools expose the same operations. Detailed sharing controls and adding without a current project remain open. Confirmed under RAG-11.

decisions.source: User: name has been settled. DevWorks.
decisions.decision: The confirmed product name is DevWorks. Replace provisional Superharness branding in current requirements and the mock UI. Legacy local requirement URLs remain compatible; canonical deliverables use devworks-requirements.

decisions.source: User: the repository is at ~/repos/devworks. Local Git verified the canonical path and origin.
decisions.decision: Use /Users/michael/Repos/DevWorks, origin https://github.com/SceneWorks/DevWorks, as the project repository and canonical home for local planning. Store planning artifacts in docs/planning and authoring sources in tools/planning. The future app updater reads GitHub Releases from SceneWorks/DevWorks; this planning change does not configure or run an updater.

decisions.source: User: Yes to keeping a managed copy; imported documents should be considered project artifacts.
decisions.decision: Every imported knowledge document is a DevWorks-managed project artifact. Index/retrieve its managed copy independently of the original external path, retaining source provenance and applicable project/feature/task links. Existing artifact retention, sharing, identity and deletion rules apply; index removal alone does not delete the artifact. Confirmed under RAG-12.

decisions.source: User: macOS 26.2, Windows 10; Linux whatever can be supported.
decisions.decision: Minimum OS targets are macOS 26.2 and Windows 10. Linux remains required, with distribution/version coverage to be proposed and validated during architecture work. CPU architectures and packaging remain open. Record actual compatibility rather than promising all Linux distributions. PLAT-01.

decisions.source: User generally grants agents full access; other users may want restrictions, so make access configurable. Add basic checks preventing accidental deletion of drives or repositories.
decisions.decision: Support configurable broad/full and restricted agent access. The user’s personal full-access preference does not choose a universal initial default. Basic destructive-tool-call guards remain active in full-access mode, protecting whole drives and repositories; existing reviewer read-only and approval/main protection rules remain effective. Scope/defaults, deliberate exception policy and practical enforcement including arbitrary native executables remain architecture decisions. SEC-03–04 confirmed; SEC-05 proposed mechanics.

decisions.source: User: Agreed on recovery, accepting reconciliation before retry and escalation of unresolved uncertainty while unrelated work continues.
decisions.decision: Reconcile interrupted pushes, merges, database writes and other state-changing tool outcomes before retrying. Do not repeat confirmed completed effects or blindly replay uncertain mutations. Escalate unresolved outcomes, holding affected/dependent work only; unrelated work continues. Existing lifecycle/manual-resume policy remains effective. STORE-04 confirmed.

decisions.source: User: clean purposeful architecture, avoid redundant code, focus on reuse and testability throughout.
decisions.decision: Make component responsibilities, dependency directions and ownership explicit; reuse established shared behavior while avoiding duplicated logic/state, speculative frameworks and unnecessary abstractions. Important logic must be testable through explicit boundaries independently of UI and real inference. ARCH-07–08 confirmed.

decisions.source: User: well documented code so agents understand every piece; visual documents for objects, interfaces, inheritance and major/difficult workflows such as plugins.
decisions.decision: Require useful source/module/type/trait/API documentation, maintained guides and versioned editable/rendered visual design documents. Show actual Rust structures, interfaces/trait implementations, ownership/composition and applicable inheritance/supertrait relationships. Major workflows and plugin lifecycle/protocol/capabilities/approval/failure/updates need visual explanations. Keep proposed and implemented designs distinct. DOC-01–02 and VIS-01–03 confirmed.

decisions.source: User explicitly corrected the initial wording: integration tests must NOT use real inference; later separate end-to-end tests will. Unit tests are integral, all important code testable, with no coverage percentage.
decisions.decision: Require meaningful unit tests and full deterministic integration tests of component interactions, without live-provider calls or local model inference. Use controlled provider/stream/tool fixtures and exercise real local components where relevant. No numerical coverage threshold. Real inference is reserved for a distinct end-to-end suite to be set up later, with separate entry points/configuration; do not treat skipped/unavailable runs as passed live validation. TEST-01–04 confirmed. This correction supersedes the earlier request wording about integration tests invoking real inference.

decisions.source: User requested an app-level toolbar chat sidebar on all screens, reusing the current Home session and posting navigation notices with Help/tool discovery; keep open until explicitly closed or Home is opened.
decisions.decision: UI-11–13 and COORD-09–10 confirmed. Use the same conversation, model pin, attachments and draft as Home; keep distinct feature/issue chats. Persist the sidebar across navigation and close on Home. Append host-attributed screen notices to the current Home transcript, with local Help references and enabled-tool discovery, preserving permission/approval boundaries and session history. Bounded payload and responsive layout/delivery mechanics remain design details.

decisions.source: User correction during architecture planning, 1 November 2026
decisions.decision: The intended conditional graph-database indexing target is HelixDB, not HydraDB. Apply the prior read-only inspection and metadata-only retention requirements to HelixDB. SQLite, MariaDB/MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server remain target engines. Validate HelixDB metadata discovery, source permissions and actual adapter coverage; do not carry over HydraDB-specific MCP/Cypher feasibility claims. Historical answers are retained above as superseded.

decisions.source: User architecture discussion, 1 November 2026
decisions.decision: If HelixDB cannot be embedded suitably, the user may prefer all-SQLite storage using graph/vector capabilities. This is a candidate fallback and reopens dependency selection; it is not a decision to replace HelixDB. Distinguish database-engine embedding from storing/searching model embeddings. HelixDB vector support is documented; its upstream embedded feature still needs dependency/platform validation.

decisions.source: User: Let us exclude Kuzu, it is a dead project.
decisions.decision: Exclude KuzuDB from active storage evaluation and implementation choices. Evaluate OverGraph, Grafeo, HelixDB and SQLite graph/vector storage; OverGraph is a promising candidate to test, not an approved winner.

decisions.source: User, 1 November 2026: use SQLite with add-ons for graph and vector storage after the local comparison.
decisions.decision: Select SQLite as the DevWorks app storage engine, replacing the initial HelixDB plus SQLite direction. Preserve graph/vector/analysis requirements. No correctness failures were detected in the tested SQLite configuration; this is not a claim that SQLite or extensions are bug-free. Specific graph extension selection remains open while GraphQLite is assessed; sqlite-vec is the measured vector-extension baseline. External HelixDB schema indexing remains a separate conditional target capability.

decisions.source: User, 1 November 2026: stick with plain SQLite and sqlite-vec; isolate storage behind repository interfaces.
decisions.decision: Select plain SQLite application-owned graph tables and sqlite-vec; exclude GraphQLite as an app dependency. Use domain-focused Rust traits and an explicit transaction contract so consumers do not directly call SQLite. Alternate backend requires adapter and validated migration/conformance, not consumer rewrites. Concrete trait names, worker handoff and physical partitioning remain architecture proposals.

decisions.source: User, 1 November 2026: Yes, paused work should require explicit Continue, including from agents and schedules.
decisions.decision: Paused work requires an explicit, authorized Continue. Start through the UI, an agent or a schedule must leave the pause effective and explain that Continue is required. Existing manual-resume requirements, permissions and other holds remain effective. This does not grant agents or schedules new authority to resume human-held work. Default parent Continue scope subsequently confirmed under continue_root_and_eligible_descendants; the later no_manual_child_pauses clarification removes the premise of separately paused children. Confirmed under CONTROL-12.

decisions.source: User, 1 November 2026: Yes, Continue should resume the coordinator and all eligible descendants while preserving separate child pauses and other blockers.
decisions.decision: Continue on a feature or standalone issue resumes its coordinator and all eligible descendant assignments, including nested assignments, preserving child-specific blockers and rechecking eligibility. The subsequent no_manual_child_pauses clarification supersedes the prior manual-child-pause interpretation. Confirmed under CONTROL-13; concrete hold storage remains open.

decisions.source: User, 1 November 2026: There won't be any manual child pauses though.
decisions.decision: Child assignments have no manual pause control. This corrects the previous discussion of separately imposed manual child pauses. Continue feature/issue still resumes its coordinator and eligible descendants, preserving child-specific blockers such as approval waits, dependencies and uncertain outcomes. CONTROL-13 clarified. The later feature_issue_manual_control_scope decision confirms removal of the independent manual child-Continue workflow.

decisions.source: User, 1 November 2026: Sounds good, what is next, accepting the preceding feature/issue control recommendation after clarifying no manual child pauses.
decisions.decision: Manual Pause/Continue operates at feature/standalone-issue scope and covers the coordinator and descendants. No independent manual child Continue control or deferred child resume workflow is required. Children wait on their own blockers; after a blocker clears, recheck eligibility and continue if the parent permits execution and other conditions allow. A paused parent keeps its children stopped. Resume authority and concrete hold mechanics remain open.

decisions.source: User, 1 November 2026: Only when explicitly authorized, answering whether agents and schedules may Continue human-paused work autonomously or only with explicit user authorization.
decisions.decision: Agents and schedules may Continue human-paused feature/issue work only with explicit user authorization. An agent can carry out an explicit user resume instruction; tool access, broad role authority or permission to start eligible new work alone does not authorize clearing a human pause. Existing app-reopen and budget manual-resume requirements and other blockers remain effective. CONTROL-12 clarified. Concrete authorization binding/lifetime and hold-clearance transactions remain architectural work.

decisions.source: User, 1 November 2026: Only approved for implementation, answering whether next_work may select incompletely planned features or only implementation-approved features.
